title: Tensorflow Recommenders (TFRS): Intro, and Building a Retrieval Stage

cues.en: Let's talk about the new Tensor flow recommender system, TFRS. It comes to you, straight from Google and tensorflow.org.
cues.zh: 談談新的 TensorFlow Recommenders，簡稱 TFRS，直接來自 Google 與 tensorflow.org。

cues.en: So I was originally going to put this under a bleeding edge alert.
cues.zh: 原本打算放進前沿研究提醒。

cues.en: But given that it's coming from Google, it's probably safe to say it works well and it's going to go mainstream.
cues.zh: 但既然來自 Google，大概可以說，運作良好，也將成為主流。

cues.en: So we'll just talk about it, because I think this is going to be an important technology going forward in the world of recommender systems.
cues.zh: 所以直接介紹，因為我認為，這會是推薦系統未來的重要技術。

cues.en: As I said, it is from Google and builds on some recent work from Google Research. And it is built on top of Keras.
cues.zh: 如前所說，來自 Google，建立在 Google Research 近期研究上，也建立在 Keras 之上。

cues.en: So all that time we spent learning about Keras in the previous section should pay off for you here.
cues.zh: 因此，上一節花時間學 Keras，現在有回報。

cues.en: Pretty thin layer on top of Keras too.
cues.zh: 而且，只在 Keras 上加很薄一層。

cues.en: So if you know how to use Keras, pretty easy to use TFRS you'll find.
cues.zh: 會用 Keras，就會發現 TFRS 很容易。

cues.en: It's pretty easy to use because Keras itself is easy to use, but also highly flexible.
cues.zh: 容易使用，因為 Keras 本身容易，也高度彈性。

cues.en: It just gives you these new tools to use within Keras really that are relevant to recommender systems.
cues.zh: 其實只是提供 Keras 內，與推薦系統相關的新工具。

cues.en: So it's not really boxing you into a specific algorithm.
cues.zh: 不會把你限制在特定演算法。

cues.en: You have a lot of flexibility to develop your own algorithms and extend them and mix them together in novel ways.
cues.zh: 能很有彈性，開發自己的演算法、擴充，以新方式混合。

cues.en: And we'll explore that a little bit more deeper here.
cues.zh: 接著會深入一點。

cues.en: So TFRS is built around this idea of having two stages to recommendations, and this is nothing new, you see this in some other research, too.
cues.zh: TFRS 圍繞兩階段推薦概念，這不是新想法，其他研究也有。

cues.en: There's basically a retrieval stage whose job is to select candidates for recommendations.
cues.zh: 第一是檢索階段，任務是選出推薦候選。

cues.en: So for a given user, what items might they be interested in?
cues.zh: 對某位使用者，可能對哪些項目感興趣？

cues.en: And the retrieval stage might select a very large number of candidates, and I might have to go through an awful lot of information to do so.
cues.zh: 檢索可能選出很多候選，也可能得處理大量資訊。

cues.en: So this tends to be where the real heavy lifting happens.
cues.zh: 因此，真正繁重工作通常在這裡。

cues.en: So we need to keep the retrieval stage kind of simple because it operates at a very large scale typically.
cues.zh: 因為通常規模很大，檢索要維持簡單。

cues.en: And then we have a separate ranking stage that takes those candidates that came out of the retrieval stage and ranks them and gives a year top end results or what have you.
cues.zh: 接著獨立排序階段，接受檢索候選，排序，給出 Top-N 結果等。

cues.en: And because that's operating on a smaller set of data, it gives us the flexibility to do more complicated things to arrive at the best final candidates for recommendations.
cues.zh: 因為處理資料較少，有彈性做更複雜的事，找出最後最佳推薦。

cues.en: You might be using a deeper neural network or fancier algorithms or something like that.
cues.zh: 也許用更深神經網路，或更精細演算法。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: But let's talk about the retrieval stage first.
cues.zh: 但先談檢索。

cues.en: So you see on the right here, this diagram, they call this a two tower model where basically we have a query model and a candidate model.
cues.zh: 右邊的圖，稱為雙塔模型，基本上有查詢模型與候選模型。

cues.en: And in these diagrams, I'm working from the top down, which is a little bit backwards from some diagrams you might see.
cues.zh: 這些圖，從上往下看，與有些圖方向相反。

cues.en: So on the query side, we're taking all the user IDs.
cues.zh: 查詢側，取所有使用者 ID。

cues.en: If we're going to take this in the context of movie lines, for example, where we're recommending movies for users, we convert all of those user IDs, the unique user I.D. to integers, and then we would
cues.zh: 例如放在 MovieLens 推薦電影情境，把所有不同使用者 ID，轉成整數，再

cues.en: put that into an embedding layer.
cues.zh: 送進嵌入層。

cues.en: And for the candidate model side for that tower, we would do the same thing for movie IDs, convert all the unique movie ideas to integers and feed those into an embedded layer as well.
cues.zh: 候選塔，對電影 ID 做相同事，把不同 ID 轉整數，也送進嵌入層。

cues.en: The underlying TFRS model will take both of those models as an input, the Query model and the candidate model.
cues.zh: 底層 TFRS 模型，接受兩個模型：查詢與候選。

cues.en: In our case, the query model is user based and the candidate model is movie based.
cues.zh: 這裡，查詢基於使用者，候選基於電影。

cues.en: Multiply them together to come up with an affinity score.
cues.zh: 將兩者相乘，得到關聯度分數。

cues.en: So as you train it with specific user movie pairs that make up an individual rating, those embedding layers get populated.
cues.zh: 以構成個別評分的使用者／電影配對訓練，嵌入層逐漸填入。

cues.en: We have these affinity scores being created for user movie pairs and we can use that to do a sort of a first pass at ranking our recommendation candidates.
cues.zh: 產生使用者／電影配對關聯度，能用來做候選的初步排序。

cues.en: So how does this work?
cues.zh: 如何運作？

cues.en: Like just looking at this.
cues.zh: 光看這個，

cues.en: It's not obvious, right?
cues.zh: 不明顯，對吧？

cues.en: Because a lot of times you think of an embedding layer is just a way of encoding.
cues.zh: 因為常把嵌入層，當作編碼方法。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: A way of forcing categorical data into some sort of a standard format that can be easily fed into a neural network.
cues.zh: 將類別資料強制轉成某種標準格式，方便輸入神經網路。

cues.en: And usually that's how it's used.
cues.zh: 通常這樣使用。

cues.en: But embedding layers are more than that.
cues.zh: 但嵌入層不只如此。

cues.en: The way they're working under the hood is every unique ID is being mapped to a vector of and dimensions, maybe as 32 dimensions, 64 dimensions, whatever it is.
cues.zh: 內部，將每個唯一 ID，對應到 N 維向量，可能 32 維、64 維，不管多少。

cues.en: But it's going to be like a vector of 32 floating point values.
cues.zh: 例如，32 個浮點數的向量。

cues.en: And you can think of this as the position in a 32 dimensional space that represents the similarity between one user I.D. and another or between one movie ID and another.
cues.zh: 能視為 32 維空間的位置，代表不同使用者 ID，或不同電影 ID 之間的相似度。

cues.en: So by using embedding layers in this way, we're kind of getting around that whole problem of data sparsity and sparse vectors and at the same time getting a measure of similarity out of the deal as well.
cues.zh: 因此，這樣用嵌入層，一方面繞過稀疏資料、稀疏向量問題，一方面也得到相似度衡量。

cues.en: So it's a very simple and straightforward way of getting a first cut at your recommendation candidates.
cues.zh: 是產生初步推薦候選，非常簡單直接的方法。

cues.en: So that's what's going on here.
cues.zh: 這就是這裡發生的事。

cues.en: So then we could just brute force sort them all and get our top recommendations and we could call it done at that point and just say, hey, we have recommendations now just from the retrieval stage.
cues.zh: 接著，可以暴力排序，取得最佳推薦，就算完成，說我們只靠檢索階段，就有推薦了。

cues.en: But there's more typically there's going to be a ranking stage as well.
cues.zh: 但還有，通常也會有排序階段。

cues.en: But before we go on to ranking, let's dive into the retrieval stage in more depth and actually do a code walk through here and run some code that shows you how it all works in practice.
cues.zh: 繼續排序前，更深入檢索，真正走過程式碼，執行範例，看實務運作。
